CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male with a past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension who presents with an upper respiratory infection. Over the past week, while working in the yard performing landscaping, he began experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath. He believes he caught his first cold at the end of summer after not consistently wearing masks. Shortness of breath has been exertional, particularly when lifting or carrying heavy bags of soil. He denies productive cough at this time but anticipates developing one. He reports mild subjective fever, which he attributed to exertion. He also reports bilateral elbow pain and knee soreness associated with the physical work. The patient has received both COVID vaccines.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for fatigue, exertional dyspnea, mild subjective fever, and bilateral elbow and knee pain. Denies productive cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or seasonal allergies.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Depression
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
3. Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin (to be increased to 1000 mg twice daily)

ALLERGIES
No seasonal allergies. No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works during the week. He performs landscaping and yard work. He attends social gatherings. His wife encourages participation in barre classes for relaxation, which he finds helpful. He monitors blood pressure and glucose levels more regularly during work weeks but inconsistently on weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Within normal limits, afebrile
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds strong and regular
Respiratory: Scattered rhonchi bilaterally that clear with cough
Extremities: Mild bilateral lower extremity edema; bilateral elbow tenderness to palpation

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease or pneumonia
Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0 (elevated; target 6-7)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper Respiratory Infection/Viral Syndrome: Presumed viral etiology. COVID-19 test to be sent. Expected resolution within a couple of days. Treatment: Robitussin for cough; ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed for fever and pain.

2. Depression: Patient currently doing well with stress management through barre classes. Offered medical management or psychotherapy referral. Patient declined at this time; to reassess in a few months.

3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8.0 (goal 6-7). Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1C in 4 months. Continue dietary modification and glucose monitoring.

4. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Lisinopril refill ordered. Lipid panel ordered. Encourage continued home blood pressure monitoring.

Follow-up appointment in 4 months. Patient instructed to call if symptoms worsen.
